identity: Exact per-file hashes bind the inspected candidate; the local-server source differs from the parent only in an independent test expectation. This is a historical snapshot, not a claim that future HEAD matches.

inputs: every tracked desktop/shell file, including non-literal modules, ACLs and binary assets
explicit Panel context and shell bridge consumers

findings.finding: 37 of 74 owned files have no expanded lexical/path match. Whole-crate ownership, generated command ACLs, certificate helpers and assets must be accounted for separately.
Native IPC, Tauri drag hit regions, overlay titlebar geometry, microphone permission policy and Gateway filesystem access are distinct roles. Do not widen them using one blanket marker replacement.
The tauri scheme branch is live Gateway compatibility behavior, not a historical string. Core remains its authority; no trust-policy change is made in this slice.

The retained native notification route chooses registered ai.aleph.desktop / ai.aleph.panel AUMIDs, then Aleph fallback. NSH packaging must validate this identity relationship; deleting the Windows capability is not a valid migration.
A reference to the old desktop certificate store describes a shared trust representation; it is not evidence that the iOS implementation is Tauri-owned.
A native window_drag view property exists. Equivalent behavior for Panel DOM data-tauri-drag-region attributes has not been demonstrated; no no-op attribute substitution is accepted.

limitations: Lexical/path discovery does not prove transitive dependency or feature closure. Dynamic path construction and indirect consumers still need build/graph checks at P11-G.
Source hashes and line anchors do not prove rendered UI, actual native effects, restart/rollback, cross-platform parity or a 14-day run.
Commands and lifecycle migration dispositions remain in the canonical phase11-nsh-inventory.json; this census is evidence, not a second command authority.
